I implemented `tax_for` in `src/billing/tax.py` with half-up rounding. I haven't run it or added tests.

The function was a `NotImplementedError` stub, so there was no existing rounding to change. It now multiplies integer cents by the rate as a `Decimal`, rounds with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, and returns integer cents. No floats are involved. For example, 1050 cents at a 5% rate gives 52.5, which rounds to 53 (half-even would give 52).

I also updated EngramDB. The old "Tax uses ROUND_HALF_EVEN" memory (March 2026 decision, which explicitly said not to use half-up) is now flagged as challenged, using your statement as evidence. A new half-up decision memory replaces it.

It was already challenged, and my replacement was created in the same batch. I would have wanted the hook to omit or annotate challenged and superseded memories, for example with a "challenged" marker.

3. **Truncated previews.** The hazard and convention memories were cut short. I didn't need them for this task, so I didn't call `get`. A full-text option on the hook injection would have been convenient.
